title.value: A Tight and Unified Analysis of Gradient-Based Methods for a Whole Spectrum of Differentiable Games
title.justification: The title is explicitly stated at the beginning of the provided paper text.
title.quote: A Tight and Unified Analysis of Gradient-Based Methods for a Whole Spectrum of Differentiable Games

analysis.description: The paper provides a comprehensive analysis of gradient-based methods, specifically extragradient (EG), optimistic gradient method (OG), and consensus optimization (CO), for finding Nash equilibria in differentiable games. It offers new insights into the convergence rates of these methods across different game settings, from bilinear to strongly monotone games. The paper aims to provide a unified framework for understanding the dynamics of these gradient-based methods and their advantages over traditional gradient descent (GD).

type.justification: The paper focuses on providing theoretical analyses of convergence rates and frameworks for gradient-based methods in differentiable games, rather than experimental or empirical evaluations.
type.quote: We provide new analyses of the EG’s local and global convergence properties and use is to get a tighter global convergence rate for OG and CO.
